title: observability: token-level metrics/tracing/logging dashboard enhancements and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Enhance token-level metrics, tracing and logging dashboards; tune alerts to reduce noise and improve signal for KV cache and token-cost regressions.
description:
Motivation: Customers and SREs continue to ask for finer-grained observability into token-level costs and latency, KV cache behavior, and request-level traces to diagnose tail-latency regressions. Previous dashboards gave good aggregate visibility but made it difficult to correlate token-level cost spikes with cache miss patterns and scheduling anomalies. This change adds expanded token-level metrics, end-to-end tracing hooks, additional structured logs, dashboard improvements, and an alert tuning pass to reduce false positives while preserving high-signal alerts.

Summary of changes: 
- New Prometheus metrics: redwood_tokens_total_by_model, redwood_token_cost_usd, redwood_token_latency_ms, redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio (token-level histograms and labels by model, route, deployment region, and quantization profile).
- Tracing: instrumented request lifecycle to attach token-level cost/latency spans and KV cache decision spans to existing distributed traces (OpenTelemetry).
- Logging: structured log fields added for token_count, token_cost, kv_cache_hit, schedule_decision, batch_id to simplify join across logs/traces/metrics.
- Dashboards: consolidated token-level cost/latency dashboard with new panels for per-model token-cost breakdown, KV cache heatmap, slow-token tail traces, and token-cost anomaly chart.
- Alert tuning: modified threshold logic and added aggregation windows for alerts: token-cost-regression-high (warn/critical), kv-cache-degradation, token-latency-tail. Reduced alert chattiness by adding dynamic baselining and suppression on known maintenance windows.
- Backwards compatibility: metrics and logs are additive; previous dashboards continue to work.

Testing and validation: 
- Unit tests added for new metric formatting and tracing hooks.
- Integration tests run against perf-canary staging: simulated workloads across models (redwood-13b, rw-7b, rw-3b) to verify token cost attribution and KV cache labeling.
- Dashboard and alert preview tested with synthetic anomalies to confirm behavior and verify suppression logic.

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge to main behind feature flag token_observability_v2.
2) Gradual rollout to perf-canary and a single dedicated customer cluster for 48 hours.
3) Monitor alert rate and dashboards; adjust thresholds if needed.
4) Full rollout after 7 days or earlier with sign-off from SRE and product.

Related: ENG-5321 (token-level observability epic), ENG-5400 (kv cache metrics), PM-221 (customer request for per-token cost breakdown).

review_comments: Carlos Mendez (reviewer): Can we ensure cardinality stays bounded for model+route labels? Suggest collapsing quantization_profile into a 'quant_profile' tag with limited buckets.
Author (Aisha): Agreed, implemented a quant_profile mapping and added a cardinality test in token_metrics_test.go - reduces unique label values by ~90% in sim tests.
Lena Zhou (reviewer): Alert thresholds look reasonable, but prefer adding temporary noise suppression during autoscaling events to prevent alert storms.
Author (Aisha): Added suppression windows tied to autoscaler events and a soft-failback that shifts alerts to warning for 10m during scale-up. Documented behavior in infra/alerts/README.
Ethan Brooks (reviewer): Tracing spans are great - please confirm sampling rate won't overload Jaeger in high RPS workloads.
Author (Aisha): Set default trace sampling to 0.1% and added dynamic sampling rule for anomalies. Integration tests include high-RPS scenario to validate Jaeger ingress.
QA (comment): Ran perf-canary for 24h against rw-13b workload; token metrics and dashboards matched expected baselines. Observed 2 alerts during simulated anomaly window - both correctly classified.
notes_on_rollout: Feature gated via token_observability_v2 flag. Gradual rollout recommended: perf-canary -> single dedicated -> global. Monitor token-cost-regression-high and kv-cache-degradation alerts closely for first 72 hours and be prepared to lower sampling if tracing ingestion approaches quota.
